title: Who is making money from this war?
gist: Foreign Policy video landing page (Kyla Scanlon, 29 July 2026) asking who profits from the U.S.–Iran war; the captured text contains no transcript — only FP’s nav, featured and related-story modules. What is extractable is the dated state of the world those modules encode: Khamenei is dead, the Iran war is FP’s dominant beat, Andy Burnham is Britain’s new prime minister, and Scanlon’s own running theses are that China is winning the AI energy race and that AI won’t stay cheap.

insights.claim: Iranian state media confirmed the death of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and funeral ceremonies for him were held at the Grand Mosalla in Tehran on July 5, 2026.
insights.speaker: Kyla Scanlon
insights.so_what: A succession vacuum atop Iran’s clerical system is the key variable for the oil risk premium and for whether any U.S.-Iran settlement survives the transition.
insights.quote: Mourners attend a memorial vigil after Iranian state media confirmed the death of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran.

insights.claim: Foreign Policy contributors argue that the destruction of Iranian civilian life under Trump’s campaign is strengthening the Islamic Republic’s regime rather than eroding it.
insights.speaker: Kyla Scanlon
insights.so_what: Regime-collapse trades are the wrong expression; a rallying-round-the-flag Iran implies a longer conflict and a persistent energy risk premium.
insights.quote: Trump’s Destruction of Iranian Life Is Strengthening the Regime

themes.theme: Scanlon on AI cost and power

insights.claim: Kyla Scanlon’s stated position is that China is winning the AI energy race — the contest is being decided on power generation, not only on chips.
insights.speaker: Kyla Scanlon
insights.so_what: Argues for Chinese grid/generation capex and for U.S. datacenter power as the binding bottleneck rather than semiconductor supply.
insights.quote: China is winning the AI energy race

insights.claim: Kyla Scanlon argues that AI will not be cheap forever, implying today’s model and inference pricing is a subsidised, non-durable steady state.
insights.speaker: Kyla Scanlon
insights.so_what: Watch for margin compression at AI-dependent application companies whose unit economics assume today’s token prices persist.

insights.claim: Andy Burnham has become Britain’s new prime minister.
insights.speaker: Kyla Scanlon
insights.so_what: A Burnham premiership resets UK fiscal and EU-alignment expectations — directly relevant to gilts, sterling, and the live question of the U.K. rejoining the EU.
insights.quote: Who is Andy Burnham, Britain’s new prime minister?
